title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
hook: How does a model decide which words to focus on? Scaled dot-product attention computes similarity scores, turns them into weights, and mixes values. Edit the matrices to see it in action.

symbols.meaning: Normalizes each row to sum to 1

explorations.title: Equal scores
explorations.predict: If all scores are equal, what will the attention weights be?
explorations.observe: All weights become 0.5, so the output is the average of the two value vectors.
explorations.why: When scores are equal, softmax gives uniform weights. The output is the weighted sum of V with equal weights.

explorations.title: Dominant score
explorations.predict: If one score is much larger than the other, what happens to the weights?
explorations.observe: The weight for the matching key becomes close to 1, and the output is almost the corresponding value vector.
explorations.why: A large score gap makes the softmax concentrate on the largest score, so the output is dominated by the corresponding value.

self_tests.name: Output equals weighted sum of V
self_tests.expect: approx(out.output[0][0], out.weights[0][0]*inp.V[0][0] + out.weights[0][1]*inp.V[1][0], 1e-6) && approx(out.output[0][1], out.weights[0][0]*inp.V[0][1] + out.weights[0][1]*inp.V[1][1], 1e-6)

self_tests.name: No scaling gives raw dot product

limitation: This demo uses tiny 2x2 matrices and does not include multiple attention heads, masking, or training. It only illustrates the core computation of scaled dot-product attention.
misconception: Attention weights are not learned parameters; they are computed from the inputs. The scaling factor prevents large dot products from making softmax too sharp.

claims.text: The scaling factor is 1/sqrt(d_k) where d_k is the key dimension.
In this toy setup, we use 2x2 matrices and no masking or multiple heads.

outcomes.outcome: Compute similarity scores between queries and keys.
Apply softmax to get attention weights that sum to 1.
Compute the output as a weighted sum of values.
Explain the effect of scaling on the softmax distribution.
